- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.22) and price is rising, model may lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to align with sentiment shift.
- In low-volatility or mean-reverting regimes (e.g., 65–70 range), model often overpredicts; cap forecast at +2% above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses tail risks or sudden reversals; add 1–3% buffer for downside risk if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.17) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; use weighted average of recent 5-day and 15-day trends for correction.
